newsitem.title: USA: Georgia-Pacific results plunge, hurt by low prices.
newsitem.headline: Georgia-Pacific results plunge, hurt by low prices.

text.p: Georgia-Pacific Corp. said Thursday that its fourth-quarter profit fell by 99 percent as the prices of most of its wood-based products collapsed.
The Atlanta-based forest products company said its net income for the last three months of 1996 fell to $2 million, or 2 cents a share, from $197 million, or $2.17 a share.
The company said that in addition to the collapse in prices its results were also hurt by charges it took for restructuring in several divisions.
Sales slipped to $3.20 billion from $3.42 billion.
For the full year the company said its net income plunged to $156 million, or $1.72 a share, from a record $1.02 billion, or $11.29 a share.
The company said its full-year results included $20 million of expenses related to an early retirement programme and a $5 million loss from the retirement of $150 million in debt.
Annual sales fell to $13.02 billion from $14.31 billion.
Georgia-Pacific said total operating profit dwindled to $914 million from $2.29 billion, with pulp and paper business operating profits slipping to $390 million from $1.6 billion in 1995.

Profits from the building products business fell to $516 million from $669 million. The company said the unit was hurt by reduced profits in structural panels, resulting primarily from excess capacity and lower prices.
The company also said it had identified and implemented measures that will add $200 million to annual pretax earnings -- half its goal of $400 million.
It said it expects to meet the other half of its pretax earnings goal from investments in information systems, and efficiencies and cost savings in its distribution business.
Georgia-Pacific stock rose 75 cents to $78.125 at midday on the New York Stock Exchange.
